content: The recommended dose of sodium is 7 mEq per kilogram of body weight. For a 70 kg patient, this corresponds to a total volume of 3500 mL. Initially, administer 10-20 mL via slow intravenous infusion and closely monitor for any signs of an anaphylactoid reaction. This solution is used as a plasma volume substitute for both the treatment and prevention of hypovolemia. In pediatric patients, the dosage should be tailored to the individual’s specific colloid requirements, taking into account the underlying disease, hemodynamic status, and hydration levels. For newborns and infants under 2 years of age, the average dose is 16 mL/kg administered intravenously. For children aged 2-12 years, the average dose is 36 mL/kg intravenously. As with adults, begin with an initial 10-20 mL slow IV infusion and monitor for anaphylactoid reactions. Potential adverse effects include pruritus, increased serum amylase levels, reduced coagulation factors, decreased hematocrit, and anaphylactoid reactions. Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) should not be used in critically ill adults, including those with sepsis, as its use has been associated with an increased risk of mortality and the need for renal replacement therapy. HES is contraindicated in critically ill adults (including those with sepsis), patients with severe liver disease, hypersensitivity to the product, conditions associated with volume overload, pre-existing coagulation or bleeding disorders, renal failure with oliguria or anuria not related to hypovolemia, patients undergoing dialysis, severe hypernatremia or hyperchloremia, and intracranial bleeding. Anaphylactoid reactions, which may present as mild influenza-like symptoms, bradycardia, tachycardia, bronchospasm, or non-cardiac pulmonary edema, have been reported. Avoid using HES in patients with pre-existing renal dysfunction, and discontinue its use at the first sign of renal injury. Renal function should be monitored for at least 90 days following administration. In patients undergoing open-heart surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass, monitor coagulation status closely, as excessive bleeding has been reported with HES solutions in this population. Discontinue use at the first sign of coagulopathy. To prevent fluid overload, adjust the dosage in patients with cardiac or renal dysfunction. In cases of severe dehydration, administer a crystalloid solution first. During prolonged parenteral therapy or when clinically indicated, monitor fluid balance, serum electrolytes, renal and hepatic function, acid-base balance, and coagulation parameters. HES is classified as Pregnancy Category C. It is unknown whether the drug is excreted in human breast milk. Approximately 62-70% of the administered dose is excreted in the urine over 72 hours. The information provided here is for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual treatment plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Always consult the applicable healthcare provider or plan for the most current information.
